Diagnosis.Molecular Markers: ER negative, PR negative, HER2 negative (IHC 0; FISH ratio 1.7)

Surgery Information.Surgery Procedure: right breast simple mastectomy and sentinel lymph node biopsy
Surgery Information.Surgery Findings: 3.6 cm of grade 3 IDC, mitotic count was quite elevated at 74/10 hpf, final margins were negative, features suggestive of lymphovascular invasion were present, no DCIS was present, one of the 2 sentinel lymph nodes was positive for adenocarcinoma (1.2 cm, but no extranodal extension), estrogen receptor negative, progesterone receptor negative, HER2 positive, variable Ki67 expression (<5% to 25-30%; average ~15%)

Additional Comments: The patient is an 81-year-old postmenopausal woman with a recent diagnosis of Stage II (T2N1) triple negative breast cancer. She has multiple medical comorbidities, including congestive heart failure with a left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) of 25% and diabetes mellitus type II. She recently developed dyspnea and was managed with Lasix for her heart failure. The patient underwent a right breast simple mastectomy and sentinel lymph node biopsy, revealing a 3.6 cm grade 3 invasive ductal carcinoma (IDC) with lymphovascular invasion and one positive sentinel lymph node. The tumor is estrogen receptor negative, progesterone receptor negative, and HER2 positive with variable Ki67 expression. The patient is currently considering further staging imaging to assess for metastasis before making decisions regarding chemotherapy, given the potential risks associated with her comorbid conditions.
